newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish police charge two after anti-IRA raids.
newsitem.headline: Irish police charge two after anti-IRA raids.

text.p: Two men were charged with possessing explosives and detonating cord on Wednesday after a series of police raids that the Irish media said had foiled Irish Republican Army (IRA) bombings in Northern Ireland.
The Special Criminal Court ordered that the two men, who are from the Irish Republic, be held in custody.
Two other men arrested in a widespread security operation during the previous 48 hours were still being questioned late on Wednesday.

Police stepped up their search operations after arresting the men and seizing vital bomb-making equipment, security sources said. "Searches are still continuing in four counties," a security source told Reuters.
The discovery of quantities of home-made detonating cord packed with powerful Semtex explosive was hailed as "a body blow to IRA terrorist plans" by the Irish Independent newspaper.
The Irish Times said the operation "disrupted a major arms supply route into Northern Ireland" where IRA guerrillas are waging an armed campaign to end British rule and reunite Ireland.
The detonating cord is similar to that used in IRA bomb attacks on British targets in Northern Ireland, England and Germany last year, security sources said.

Britain and Ireland, which are trying to ease tension between the province's minority Catholics and pro-British majority Protestants, say the guerrillas must abandon violence to win a voice in peace talks.
Last week a British soldier was shot dead at a checkpoint near the frontier with Ireland and the IRA was widely blamed.
The guerrillas, who have made no comment on the shooting, say they will not consider a ceasefire before Britain has a new government. A British general election must be called by May.
